prediction.likelyOutcome: Owners are essentially certain to recover fair market value for the Strip ($40,500-$47,400), but the case's real value turns on a genuinely contested, roughly even-odds legal question -- whether Indiana's traffic-flow/circuity bar (Ensley) or the narrow Marina Entertainment highest-and-best-use exception controls the access-damages theory -- which the pending motion in limine will likely resolve before or at trial. If the access theory survives, a jury verdict in the range of the joint appraisers' ~$1.9 million report is the most probable outcome; the more aggressive $3-4.4 million individual appraisals are also live but face added appellate risk from the State's preserved continuing objection to the jury instructions.

outcome.description: The Johnson Superior Court jury awarded $680,000 to Franciscan and $1.5 million to SCP (a $2.2 million judgment), with attorney's fees awarded to both owners under Ind. Code 32-24-1-14(b) (amount not stated) and 8% prejudgment interest. The Court of Appeals reversed on November 28, 2023, holding the traffic-flow rule bars the access damages, and remanded with instructions to vacate the judgment for SCP and enter judgment for Franciscan for only the value of the strip (appraised at $40,500-$47,400), with prejudgment interest recalculated.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: only the strip taking is compensable, about $40,500-$47,400 on the record; midpoint used.
